In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of a fully automated tool, MORPHOT, to the WFC imaging of the 46 nearby WINGS clusters, to provide a morphological classification of the 39 923 cluster members.
a new approach to automated morphological classification, with its application to the WINGS cluster sample, and with the analysis of the morphological properties of galaxies in the clusters.
the application of a new tool to the automation and the quantification of the morphological classification of galaxies in clusters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, at least as far as the WINGS clusters are concerned, the morphology of the galaxies is not strongly affected by the cluster environment.

the WINGS cluster morphological fractions are consistent, within the statistical errors and the different methodologies used, with those of the field and that the fraction of early-type galaxies in clusters increases with the distance from the cluster centre, as expected.
the WINGS morphological fractions are in agreement with the literature, although we note that the fraction of S0s is lower than in the literature, whereas the fraction of spirals is higher.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a tool to automatically classify the morphologies of galaxies in the V-band WFC imaging.
MORPHOT is an effective tool for the automated morphological classification of WINGS galaxies.
we present an automatic, non-parametric tool to derive galaxy morphology from imaging data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fraction of early-type galaxies is significantly higher in clusters than in the field.
, in the WINGS cluster sample, the fraction of galaxies in the cluster outskirts is larger than that in the cluster centre for all types but S0.

, in the WINGS nearby clusters, early-type galaxies (ellipticals + S0) dominate the cluster cores (r ≤ 0.5R200) with a fraction of ∼80 per cent, while the fraction of late-type galaxies (spirals) is ∼20 per cent.
